picks.title: What's the biggest barrier to thriving? A philosopher and a space architect answer | Ariel Ekblaw and Meghan Sullivan
picks.summary: Philosopher Meghan Sullivan and space architect Ariel Ekblaw don't usually work at the same altitude ... but put them in a room together, and they'll answer the big questions. Drawing on wisdom from Aristotle to astronauts, they discuss what humans inherently owe each other, what it takes to live a good life and what a rulebook for a better world might look like. (This conversation is part of “TED Intersections,” a series featuring thought-provoking conversations between experts navigating the ideas shaping our world.) Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.
picks.reason: Philosopher discusses ethics and living well, touching on Aristotelian ideas.

picks.title: Summer Fridays: How zombies, dragons, and superheroes could make you a better person (w/ Christopher Robichaud)
picks.summary: Roleplaying games and the Marvel universe may be fictional, but they can also teach us a lot about morality in the real world. Christopher Robichaud is a Lecturer in Ethics and Public Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School of Government. In this episode, he shares ways we can explore important, everyday issues in fun, safe, and unexpected ways. Christopher has made a career out of teaching ethics and philosophy using pop culture, dissecting moral questions using anything from zombie apocalypse simulations to superhero narratives. picks.title: modern stoicism with RYAN HOLIDAY
picks.summary: Ryan Holiday explains how he discovered Stoicism and why its ideas continue to resonate today, particularly when confronting death, adversity, parenting and uncertainty. They explore memento mori as a practice for becoming more present and grateful, while distinguishing Stoic acceptance from fatalism. Kasia also reflects on how cancer led her to Stoicism as a way of managing fear and finding emotional balance.learn more about Ryan and listen to his podcast The Daily Stoicwatch this episode on YouTubeKeep up to date with Peter on SubstackKeep up to date with Kasia!Producer: Rachel BarrettThanks
picks.reason: Ryan Holiday reflects on Stoic practices confronting death, adversity, and fear.
